Enhancements: - Modify command-line argument parsing to support the new local state option - Update environment variable handling to use the new local state path ### Proposed technical implementation details ## Reviewer Guide Introducing the ability to run multiple instances of Windows Terminal with separate settings and state by using the `--localstate` command-line argument. Modify parsing to support the new local state option. The changes modify the settings path retrieval logic and window class name generation to incorporate the environment variable, allowing for isolated settings for each instance. This pull request adds support for a new command-line argument `-L` or `--localstate` to allow users to specify a custom local state directory for Windows Terminal. 📚 Docs: affected flag does not behave as expected

### What is the improvement or update you wish to see?

I would like to see a better explanation of how affected behaves, or renaming of the flag.

when I see `turbo run test --affected`, I read this as saying "run all test tasks in projects that are affected by the changes between main and HEAD"

However, what it actually means is "run all tests in projects that were changed between main and HEAD"

This is a very distinct difference. I expect `--affected` to correlate with `--filter=...[main...HEAD]` but it is actually `--filter=[main...HEAD]`

### Is there any context that might help us understand?

We have been using `--affected` in our CI workflows for months, and kept running into issues where changes to our UI library were not triggering test runs in our dependant apps. This started a whole debate around how `--affected` wasn't reliable and doesn't work. It turns out it does work as implemented, it's just the name is misleading. We have now updated our CI workflows to use `--filter=...[main...HEAD]` and are seeing the results we expected.

According to the documentation:
> Automatically filter to only packages that are affected by changes on the current branch.

If a package dependency has been changed, then the dependant package is affected by that change.

Either `--affected` was should be named `--changed`, or the documentation should be clearer. Better yet, the `--affected` implementation could be changed to do what it claims to do, and run against packages that are affected by the changes on the current branch.

### Does the docs page already exist? Please link to it.

https://turbo.build/repo/docs/reference/run#--affected

Negative wildcard env keys are not disabling framework detection (for Vite at least), the only way to opt-out that works is using the `--framework-inference=false` flag.

7. ✅ Run `VITE_FOO=5 turbo build --framework-inference=false`, `pkg-a` and `app-a` are **cache hits** (full turbo).

Watch: Support Path Pattern Matching

# Request

It would be nice if the [watch](https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/develop/#watch) `path` attribute behaved like the `ignore` attribute. For example, `path` could accept wildcards such as `*`.

At the very least it would help to have some more detail in the API documentation adding that (at least for the time being) pattern matching does not work on `path`.

Reference: https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/develop/

# Example

I would like the convenience of being able to do this:

```yaml
services:
  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "5173:5173"
    develop:
        watch:
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/*.json
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/*.js
```

instead of the verbose (yet explicit):

```yaml
services:
  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "5173:5173"
    develop:
        watch:
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/jsconfig.json
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/package-lock.json
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/package.json
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/eslint.config.js
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/svelte.config.js
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/tailwind.config.js
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/vite.config.js
```

## Nice To Have

Bonus points for allowing multiple `path` entries in a single `rebuild` action:

```yaml
services:
  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "5173:5173"
    develop:
        watch:
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/*.json frontend/*.js
```

Currently, passing a space separated list is silently interpreted as a single path. So, the below example (misleadingly) does not match `frontend/package.json` nor `frontend/vite.config.js`

```yaml
        - action: rebuild
          path: frontend/package.json frontend/vite.config.js
```

Add ElasticsearchRemoteLogIO.from_config and register elasticsearch scheme

Part of #70265 (related: #67056).

## Why

#67056 decoupled remote logging from the hardcoded branches in `airflow_local_settings.py`: core and
the Task SDK now resolve the handler via `ProvidersManager` dispatch on the
`[logging] remote_base_log_folder` URL scheme, instantiating the provider class through a no-arg
`from_config()` classmethod. This issue migrates the Elasticsearch backend.

## Design note (feedback welcome)

Unlike the object-storage backends, Elasticsearch is currently selected by `[elasticsearch] host`
being set — `remote_base_log_folder` typically has no scheme for these deployments, so pure scheme
dispatch cannot reach it. The proposal:

- Register an `elasticsearch` scheme and document setting
  `[logging] remote_base_log_folder = elasticsearch://` as the forward-looking configuration.
- Keep the legacy host-based selection working via the transitional fallback in
  `airflow_local_settings.py` until the chain is removed (tracked by the meta issue), so existing
  configs are unaffected.

## What

- [ ] Add `ElasticsearchRemoteLogIO.from_config()` in
      `providers/elasticsearch/src/airflow/providers/elasticsearch/log/es_task_handler.py`,
      mirroring the legacy branch:
      https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/104ad12e190db7197fa303d98a3ab68879eafd33/airflow-core/src/airflow/config_templates/airflow_local_settings.py#L304-L347
      — reading the `[elasticsearch]` options the branch reads (`host`, `target_index`,
      `write_stdout`, `write_to_es`, `json_format`, `log_id_template`, `host_field`,
      `offset_field`) plus `[logging] base_log_folder` (with `expanduser`) and
      `[logging] delete_local_logs`, so behavior is unchanged for existing configs. Note the legacy
      branch does *not* merge `remote_task_handler_kwargs` IO-kwargs for this backend — mirror that
      too.
- [ ] Register the `elasticsearch` scheme under a `remote-logging:` section in
      `providers/elasticsearch/provider.yaml` and mirror it in
      `providers/elasticsearch/src/airflow/providers/elasticsearch/get_provider_info.py`.
- [ ] Document the `remote_base_log_folder = elasticsearch://` form in the provider's logging docs.
- [ ] Add tests mirroring `TestS3RemoteLogIOFromConfig` in
      `providers/amazon/tests/unit/amazon/aws/log/test_s3_task_handler.py`.
- [ ] Verify end to end with a real system test: set up the actual backend yourself (a real
      Elasticsearch cluster or a local one, e.g. via Docker), run a task with remote logging
      enabled, and confirm logs are written and read back through the new dispatch path. Include
      the setup and verification results in the PR description.

## Notes

The legacy branch also swaps the `task` handler class inside `DEFAULT_LOGGING_CONFIG`; that dict is
kept only for import compatibility (see the comment at its definition in
`airflow_local_settings.py`), so `from_config` should not need to replicate it — but please verify
task-log reads work end to end with the new dispatch.

Merged examples to follow: #69817 (s3), #69816 (cloudwatch). If `from_config` raises on a bad
config, the shared factory falls back to the legacy path, so this is not a breaking change.

Unsigned .pyd files blocked by Windows WDAC code integrity policies

### Describe the issue:

NumPy's compiled extension modules (.pyd files) are not Authenticode-signed. On Windows systems with WDAC (Windows Defender Application Control) code integrity policies enforced, this causes numpy to fail to import with:

```
DLL load failed while importing _mt19937: An Application Control policy has blocked this file.
```

This is becoming increasingly common as organizations deploy WDAC policies, and it breaks any Python application that depends on numpy — even if the application only needs numpy for optional features.

### Reproduce the code example:

```python
# On a Windows system with WDAC code integrity enforced:
import numpy  # Fails with DLL load error
```

Verify that .pyd files are unsigned:
```powershell
Get-AuthenticodeSignature (Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter "*.pyd" -Path "$env:APPDATA\uv\tools\chunkhound\Lib\site-packages\numpy")
# All show Status: NotSigned
```

### Error message:

```
ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _mt19937: An Application Control policy has blocked this file.
```

### NumPy/Python version information:

- numpy 2.4.2
- Python 3.13
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100 (x64)
- WDAC CodeIntegrityPolicyEnforcementStatus = 2 (enforced)

### Context

This was reported in https://github.com/chunkhound/chunkhound/issues/192 where it crashes the MCP server at startup. The workaround is to lazy-load numpy so it's only imported when actually needed, but that doesn't help applications that require numpy at startup.

Authenticode-signing the .pyd files in the wheel build would allow numpy to work on WDAC-enforced systems. Other major projects with native extensions (e.g., some Microsoft packages) sign their DLLs for this reason.

### Related

- WDAC documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/windows-defender-application-control/wdac
- Authenticode signing: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/seccrypto/authenticode

Calling pytest.main() repeatedly (possible fix for ImportPathMismatchError)

I am using pytest to grade (a lot of) student assignments. Though documented as "not recommended" (https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/usage.html#pytest-main-usage), the benefit for me of calling a bunch of tests within the same Python process were significant enough for me to bang my head against the wall on this for a couple of days.

If you don't (or can't) call pytest using the `--import-mode=importlib` option, then in my use case you always get the dreaded `ImportPathMismatchError` exception. I'm sure I'm oversimplifying, but this is because once a module is loaded, it's cached in memory and referenced by the name of the module. Assuming the modules are just files (as will be the case with the test files) then there will be duplicates as I'm running the same test files against student projects repeatedly. And Python won't overwrite the cached modules with the new versions.

To get around this, I'm "restoring" a pre-invocation version of the in-memory modules by deleting any that are loaded during the pytest run. But it's overly complicated since I also want to optimize performance by avoiding modules that pytest needs and would have to reload. So the code looks something like this:
```python
keep_packages = ['_asyncio',
                 '_contextvars',
                 '_elementtree',
                 '_pytest',
                 '_ssl',
                 'asyncio',
                 'attr',
                 'cmd',
                 'code',
                 'codeop',
                 'contextvars',
                 'faulthandler',
                 'pdb',
                 'pkgutil',
                 'pyexpat',
                 'pytest_metadata',
                 'pytest_subtests',
                 'readline',
                 'ssl',
                 'unittest',
                 'xml']

pretest_modules = [key for key in sys.modules.keys()]

pytest.main(
    ['--tb=no', '-q']
)

posttest_modules = [key for key in sys.modules.keys()]
for module_name in posttest_modules:
    if module_name in pretest_modules:
        continue
    package = module_name.split('.')[0]
    if package in keep_packages:
        continue
    del sys.modules[module_name]
```
It works like a charm, but if something like this could be added directly to pytest.main()--perhaps as an optional argument ike `remove-loaded-modules=True` to avoid unexpected side effects for others)--it could be much more efficient. Simply capture the environment state immediately prior to invoking tests and restoring it immediately following.

And of course it could save a lot of bruised foreheads and damaged walls.

I looked at the source and was too overwhelmed to attempt a pull request. But someone familiar with it likely could make this happen quite easily if it makes sense.

Reporter updates:
[2025-02-17T15:46:19Z]
I understand the hesitance to add in maintenance. I may not have been clear since my code was complicated by a specific list of exclusions. The point was that you wouldn't need them at all if this were an embedded option. Conceptually, the code would need only be something like:
```python
if preserve_env:
    pretest_modules = [key for key in sys.modules.keys()]
    pretest_path = sys.path.copy()

# ...MODIFY PATH AND EXEC TESTS...

if preserve_env:
    posttest_modules = [key for key in sys.modules.keys() if key not in pretest_modules]
    for module_name in posttest_modules:
        del sys.modules[module_name]
    sys.path = pretest_path.copy()
```
Could even be written as a simple context manager.

Why?

1. there are times when you want in-memory access to plugins. Running tests out-of-process means that plugins have to serialize state and it must subsequently be deserialized in order to access it.
2. it's **vastly** faster than starting new processes when running potentially hundreds of short tests.
3. it makes use via API behave in a way that is consistent with how people expect, and reverts the sys "hacks" that pytest already does.

I don't see it as being overly hacky or unsafe. Discovered test files (and any additional modules loaded by the test files) will always be "last in" and should be safely deleted. At least they were in my testing. And if it's somehow unsafe for your particular test code, you just don't add the optional flag. ### 版本类型

### ⭐️ 需求描述

## 背景

当前 JumpServer 对接 **Elasticsearch 9.x** 作为命令存储时会出现：

1. **Core**：保存/校验命令存储、创建会话时报 `Unsupported ES_VERSION 9` / `invalid_elasticsearch`
2. **终端组件写 ES**：bulk 走旧接口带 `type` 参数，ES9 报错
   `unrecognized parameter: [type]`，随后回退到 default DB（日志可见 `es failure to bulk save` / `Switch default command storage` / `try to upload commands to server`）

官方说明：Elasticsearch **8.x 客户端可对接 ES 9.x 服务端**。因此可采用「识别主版本 9，复用现有 ES8 客户端路径」的最小改动，而无需引入 elasticsearch9 包（且 Python 侧 elasticsearch8 与 elasticsearch9 的 transport 依赖冲突，不宜同环境共存）。

## 目标

- 全链路支持将 **ES 9** 作为命令存储（校验、建会话、组件写入、审计查询）
- 开源组件通过 PR 合入；**企业版（xpack）组件**需研发侧同步适配

## 已完成的开源改动（共 3 处）

| # | 仓库 | 改动要点 | PR |
|---|------|----------|-----|
| 1 | `jumpserver/jumpserver`（Core） | `apps/common/plugins/es.py`：`ESClient` 工厂 `version in (8, 9)` 时复用 `ESClientV8` |   |
| 2 | `jumpserver/koko` | `pkg/proxy/recorderstorage/es.go`：`IsEs8` 识别 `8\|9`；探测失败时优先 `BulkSaveEs8`（无 `type`） |   |
| 3 | `jumpserver-dev/sdk-go` | `storage/es.go`：与 KoKo 相同逻辑（`IsEs8` 认 9 + Es8 优先） |   |

说明：

- **Lion**：依赖 sdk-go，合入 sdk-go 后重编/发版即可，无需单独造 ES 逻辑
- **Chen / Kael / Magnus（经 Wisp）**：命令写 ES 走 **Wisp → sdk-go**；sdk-go 合入后需发带新 sdk 的 **wisp**，并更新相关镜像
- 本地已验证：Core + KoKo +（replace sdk-go 的）Lion / 补丁 wisp 后，ES9 命令写入可行

## 需要研发跟进的企业版（xpack）部分

以下组件无开源修改权限，请研发在企业版仓库/镜像中同步：

### 1. Razor（客户端 RDP）— **必须改**

- 现象：命令存储指向 ES9 时日志出现
  `ES failure to bulk save: ... unrecognized parameter: [type]`，并回退 `try to upload commands to server`
- 定位：入口 `razor` 为 FreeRDP；ES 逻辑在
  **`/usr/local/razor/lib/libjumpserver.so`**（内嵌 Go / 等同 sdk-go 的 ES 客户端）
- 建议：对 `libjumpserver.so` 使用与 sdk-go 相同的 ES9 修复后重编，或依赖升级后的 sdk-go 重链

### 2. Magnus（数据库客户端代理）

- 主程序 `/opt/magnus/magnus` **未**内嵌 `IsEs8`/`BulkSaveEs` 特征
- 容器内有 **`/usr/local/bin/wisp`**，写 ES 走 Wisp
- 建议：发布/替换 **已合入 sdk-go ES9 补丁的 wisp**（与 Chen 相同），一般**不必改 Magnus 业务代码**

### 3. XRDP / 其他 xpack 图形组件（如 Nec 等）

- 请研发确认是否同样内嵌 sdk-go 或自有 ES bulk（带 `type`）
- 若有，按同一策略适配；若仅录像、不写命令 ES，可注明「无需改动」

## 建议合入/发版顺序

1. 合入 **sdk-go** ES9 补丁
2. 合入 **Core**、**KoKo**
3. 用新 sdk-go 重编 **Lion**、**Wisp**，更新 CE/EE 镜像
4. EE：重编 **Razor `libjumpserver.so`**；Magnus/Chen/Kael 镜像带上新 **wisp**
5. 文档补充：命令存储兼容 ES **7 / 8 / 9**（9 走 8.x 客户端兼容路径）

## 验证清单（供 QA）

- [ ] Core：ES9 命令存储「测试连通」成功；会话不再 `invalid_elasticsearch`
- [ ] KoKo：SSH 命令进入 ES 索引，无 `type` bulk 错误
- [ ] Lion：Web 图形键盘（回车）命令进入 ES
- [ ] Chen：Web DB SQL 命令进入 ES（依赖新 wisp）
- [ ] Magnus：客户端代理 SQL 进入 ES（依赖新 wisp）
- [ ] Razor：客户端 RDP 键盘/命令进入 ES（依赖新 `libjumpserver.so`）
- [ ] ES 7/8 回归正常

## 环境参考

- JumpServer：v4.10.17（EE）
- Elasticsearch：9.x（如 9.4.3）
- 典型失败日志：`unrecognized parameter: [type]`、`Unsupported ES_VERSION 9`

- Core: https://github.com/jumpserver/jumpserver/pull/17109
- KoKo: https://github.com/jumpserver/koko/pull/2013
- sdk-go: https://github.com/jumpserver-dev/sdk-go/pull/8/

Support ES9。
本支持方案不推荐单独增加 ESClientV9 / 引入 elasticsearch9。
单独加 elasticsearch9/ESClientV9 会与现网必装的 elasticsearch8 在 elastic-transport 上冲突，且官方已支持用 8.x 客户端连 9.x；最小、可维护的方案是复用 V8 路径，而不是再引入一套 V9 客户端。

### ⭐️ Feature Description

目前在 macOS 平台使用 JumpServerClient 连接资产时，SSH 和 SFTP 客户端支持存在一定限制。

在 Windows 平台，可以通过类似 MobaXterm 等工具同时实现 SSH 和 SFTP 连接，使用体验较为方便。

但是在 macOS 平台，目前 JumpServerClient 内置支持的 SFTP 客户端选择较少，例如默认提供的 SecureFX 等方案通常需要商业授权。对于希望使用免费工具的用户，目前缺少类似 Windows 平台 MobaXterm 的替代方案。

例如，WindTerm 是一个免费的跨平台终端工具，同时支持 SSH 和 SFTP 功能。如果 JumpServerClient 能够支持 WindTerm 作为 SSH/SFTP 调用客户端，将显著提升 macOS 用户的使用体验。

### Proposed Solution


增加对 WindTerm 的 SSH/SFTP 客户端支持；
或者开放 SSH/SFTP 客户端配置接口，允许用户自定义本地客户端路径和启动参数；
提供更加灵活的第三方客户端兼容机制，使 macOS 用户可以选择免费的 SSH/SFTP 工具。
期望效果

macOS 用户可以像 Windows 用户使用 MobaXterm 一样，通过免费的第三方工具完成：

SSH 登录 JumpServer 资产；
SFTP 文件传输；
使用统一的客户端管理远程服务器。


### Additional Information

感谢开发团队维护 JumpServer，希望后续版本能够改善 macOS 平台第三方客户端支持。

[错误报告]: Agent 核心提示词与本地插件开发 Skill 冲突，导致插件源码写入行为不一致

### 确认

- [x] 我的版本是最新版本，我的版本号与 [version](https://github.com/jxxghp/MoviePilot/releases/latest) 相同。
- [x] 我已经 [issue](https://github.com/jxxghp/MoviePilot/issues) 中搜索过，确认我的问题没有被提出过。
- [x] 我已经 [Telegram频道](https://t.me/moviepilot_channel) 中搜索过，确认我的问题没有被提出过。
- [x] 我已经修改标题，将标题中的 描述 替换为我遇到的问题。

### 当前程序版本

v2.15.1

### 运行环境

Docker

### 问题类型

主程序运行问题

### 问题描述

## 现象
- MoviePilot 内置 `skills/create-moviepilot-plugin/SKILL.md` 明确要求 Agent 查询 `PLUGIN_LOCAL_REPO_PATHS`、在本地插件仓库写入源码、构建并执行 `install_plugin(force=True)`。
- 但 `app/agent/prompt/System Core Prompt.txt` 的 `non_negotiable_boundaries` 同时规定不得通过文件编辑工具、Shell 写操作或补丁修改任何代码。
- 核心提示词优先级高于 Skill，严格执行时会导致官方插件开发 Skill 无法完成。
- 同一 `v2.15.1` 实例中曾出现不同会话行为不一致：2026-07-27 Agent 在加载长度相同的 System Core Prompt 后，仍成功使用 `write_file` / `edit_file` 修改 `PLUGIN_LOCAL_REPO_PATHS=/media/rss` 下的本地插件；当前会话则因核心规则拒绝发起源码写入。

## 复现步骤
1. 在 MoviePilot 中配置 `PLUGIN_LOCAL_REPO_PATHS`，例如 `/media/rss`。
2. 通过 Agent 明确要求创建或修改该目录下的本地插件，并选择 Vue 联邦 UI。
3. Agent 加载内置 `create-moviepilot-plugin` Skill。
4. Skill 要求写入本地插件源码，但核心系统提示词禁止修改任何代码。
5. Agent 可能拒绝写入；不同模型调用或会话也可能忽略该规则并成功写入，行为不稳定。

## 期望行为
- 明确区分 MoviePilot 核心源码与用户配置的本地插件源码。
- 禁止 Agent 修改 `/app/app` 等 MoviePilot 核心源码。
- 当管理员用户明确提出插件开发请求并加载 `create-moviepilot-plugin` Skill 时，允许写入 `PLUGIN_LOCAL_REPO_PATHS` 范围内的插件源码。
- 在 `write_file` / `edit_file` 工具后端增加路径白名单校验，避免仅依赖模型理解提示词边界。
- 增加测试，确保核心提示词与 `create-moviepilot-plugin` Skill 不互相矛盾。

## 已定位
- GitHub `v2.13.0`～`v2.13.2` 的 System Core Prompt 没有该限制。
- `v2.13.3` 提交 `f8f06a6` 以“加强 Agent 核心提示词安全约束”为由加入了禁止直接修改 application source code 的规则。
- 后续提示词重构将限制扩大为禁止修改任何 code，覆盖了本地插件源码。
- 当前 `v2.15.1` 及 GitHub 最新 `v2` 分支仍保留该规则。
- 当前 Docker 中 `/media/rss` 为 `rw` 挂载，文件系统权限不是阻塞原因。
